organizations.normalization_notes: The same historical institution may appear as either an employer or a place of study. Relationship type is stored on each affiliation; the organization sector is academia and research.
The historical corporate name and NBC abbreviation are preserved. No modern successor name is substituted.

The historically named Intelligence Corps is kept distinct from the British Army as a whole. Its parent-service relationship remains descriptive until the organization model supports parent links in reviewed imports.
Coast Guard service is modeled as a military assignment, not civilian employment. Wartime operation under Navy authority does not erase the documented Coast Guard branch.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Richard G. Arnold-Baker is very likely British Army Intelligence Corps officer Richard Gaunt Arnold-Baker.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Major (temporary) Richard Gaunt ARNOLD-BAKER ... Intelligence Corps.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The uncommon exact surname and initials, the index's British note, and the official full name, rank, branch, and wartime service number align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on an uncommon exact name plus documented British military branch and wartime context beyond the name.
claims.temporal_assessment: The officer register dates his British Army service to 1940-46, overlapping the OSS period; the exact OSS relationship remains unestablished.
claims.match_notes: Box 22 remains unreviewed. The index omits a rank and prints only British A, so the military chronology is not treated as proof of an immediate transfer.

claims.claim_text: Richard Gaunt Arnold-Baker served as a British Army Intelligence Corps officer during the war; the temporal relationship to his indexed OSS connection is uncertain.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official Gazette confirms the exact officer and Intelligence Corps; a specialized register dates service from 1940 to 1946.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity based on the uncommon name and corroborating British military evidence.
claims.temporal_assessment: The assignment is wartime and plausibly connected, but no reviewed source says it immediately preceded OSS service.
claims.match_notes: Published only as a qualified wartime affiliation. It is excluded from default confidence-aware aggregates that require confirmed or high claims.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Lieutenant Everett J. Athens is the USNR lieutenant junior grade listed as Everette J. Athens in the contemporaneous Evros Mission report.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Lt. (jg) Everette J. Athens, USNR, 2nd in command.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact surname, middle initial, naval officer grade, reserve branch, and direct OSS mission role align despite the report's extra final e.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by a contemporaneous OSS report with exact middle initial, naval grade, reserve branch, and mission role.
claims.temporal_assessment: The 1944 mission report establishes OSS service but does not document Athens's employment or assignment immediately before OSS.
claims.match_notes: Everette is retained as a documented spelling variant, not silently treated as a correction. Box 24 is needed for the pre-OSS chronology.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Clarence A. Berdahl is University of Illinois political science professor Clarence Arthur Berdahl, recruited for the OSS London staff in 1944.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Professor Clarence A. Berdahl ... has been requested by the United States Office of Strategic Services
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name, university minutes, academic title, explicit OSS request, London assignment, and institutional finding aid all align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by contemporaneous institutional minutes explicitly naming the same person and OSS assignment.
claims.temporal_assessment: The March 1944 minutes state that his university leave would begin when he departed to report for OSS duty abroad.
claims.match_notes: The finding aid independently documents 1944 London OSS service in Berdahl's papers. Box 50 remains unreviewed.

claims.claim_text: Clarence A. Berdahl's immediate pre-OSS employer was the University of Illinois, where he was professor and chair of political science.
claims.evidence_excerpt: leave of absence will become effective whenever it is necessary for him to leave the University to report for duty abroad
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Official minutes connect his current university position directly to departure for the OSS London staff.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed exact-person match in contemporaneous University of Illinois minutes.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly immediate: the leave became effective when Berdahl left the university to report abroad.
claims.match_notes: This is both the immediate pre-OSS affiliation and the last documented civilian employer before OSS service.

claims.claim_text: The University of Illinois was Clarence A. Berdahl's last documented civilian employer before OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The minutes document continuous university employment until Berdahl left to report for OSS duty, with no intervening affiliation.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed exact-person match in direct institutional records.
claims.temporal_assessment: The source explicitly ties the end of active university duties to departure for OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The employment and temporal sequence are stated in the same contemporaneous official record.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Lieutenant Colonel Hugh M. Beville is very likely NBC audience-research executive Hugh Malcolm Beville.
claims.evidence_excerpt: only leaving for a brief period during World War II to serve in the army
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and middle initial, NBC chronology, Army interruption, and indexed lieutenant-colonel Army grade align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the exact uncommon name plus documented wartime Army service and compatible chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: NBC employment began in 1930; a 1940 article confirms the role before the institutional biography's wartime Army interruption.
claims.match_notes: Box 54 remains unreviewed, so the exact Army-to-OSS sequence is not asserted.

claims.claim_text: National Broadcasting Company is the best-supported last civilian employer before Hugh M. Beville's wartime Army service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary 1940 article names Beville as NBC research manager; the museum biography says he left NBC briefly for wartime Army service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity supported by an exact uncommon name, compatible Army service, and two independent reputable sources.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded as the last civilian employer before Army service; the precise leave and OSS dates remain unknown.
claims.match_notes: NBC is not marked immediate pre-OSS because an Army assignment may have intervened.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Coast Guard Lieutenant John P. Booth is very likely John P. Booth Jr., the Coast Guard officer who commanded OSS Operational Swimmer Group II.
claims.evidence_excerpt: LT John Booth became the commander of OSG II in the CBI Theater
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and initial, Coast Guard lieutenant grade, OSS maritime command, CBI service, and Burma corroboration align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on exact name and initial plus several specific branch, rank, unit, theater, and wartime-role identifiers.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official history establishes Coast Guard assignment to OSS duty and OSG II command by 1944.
claims.match_notes: Box 68 remains unreviewed. The obituary's postwar occupation is excluded from the pre-OSS employment claim.

claims.claim_text: John P. Booth entered OSS duty as a United States Coast Guard lieutenant and later commanded Operational Swimmer Group II.
claims.evidence_excerpt: a few officers were assigned to OSS duty
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official CIA history identifies Coast Guard officers assigned to OSS duty and specifically names Lieutenant John Booth as OSG II commander.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence exact-person match based on name, Coast Guard branch, lieutenant grade, and OSS maritime command.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly immediate at the institutional level: Booth was a Coast Guard officer assigned to OSS duty.
claims.match_notes: This is a military assignment, not a civilian employer. No reliable prewar civilian employer has yet been identified.
